statements.atom: An atom is the smallest unit of an element, a positively charged nucleus surrounded by negatively charged electrons. Atoms can be subdivided, but they lose their identity in the process, and they combine to form molecules, the smallest units of compounds.
statements.brownian-motion: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of a visible particle suspended in a fluid, struck unevenly by the invisible molecules around it. It was the first direct evidence that atoms and molecules exist.
statements.size-of-atoms: Einstein’s theory of Brownian motion, with Perrin’s measurements, gives atoms a size of about $10^{-10}$ m. Knowing the size of an atom gives Avogadro’s number, since it tells how many atoms fit into a certain volume.
statements.cathode-ray-tube: In a gas discharge tube, electrons freed from the gas accelerate from the cathode to the anode, and a magnet bends their path in the direction expected for a negative charge, so cathode rays are streams of electrons.
statements.electron-charge-to-mass-ratio: Thomson measured the ratio of the electron’s charge to its mass, $\kqe/m_{\text{e}} = \ka/\kEf = -1.76 \times 10^{11}$ C/kg, using crossed electric and magnetic fields. The ratio is about a thousand times the charge per kilogram needed to plate a material, so the electron has a very small mass.
statements.millikan-oil-drop: Millikan measured the charge of the electron directly by holding a charged drop of oil still between two plates, where the electric force balances its weight. Every charge he found was a multiple of one basic charge.
statements.electron-mass: The charge from Millikan and the ratio from Thomson give the mass of the electron, $m_{\text{e}} = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$ kg, the smallest of any particle that has mass. The proton is about 1836 times heavier and carries nearly all the mass of a hydrogen atom.
statements.identical-particles: Every electron has exactly the same charge and mass; the values are not averages over many electrons. This kind of fact has no counterpart among the grains of sand or the planets of everyday physics.
statements.rutherford-scattering: In Rutherford’s gold foil experiment most alpha particles went straight through the foil, but a few came almost straight back, which only a very small, very massive, positively charged center could do. The nucleus is about $10^{-15}$ m across, 100,000 times smaller than the atom.
statements.planetary-model: In the planetary model of the atom, low-mass electrons orbit a small, massive nucleus at distances large compared with its size, held by the Coulomb force as the planets are held by gravity.
statements.discrete-atomic-spectra: An atom emits and absorbs only certain wavelengths, and each element has its own set. The lines are the atom’s fingerprint, and their discreteness means that the atom’s energies are quantized.
statements.hydrogen-spectrum-wavelengths: Every line of hydrogen’s spectrum is given by $1/\lambda = R(1/n_{\text{f}}^2 - 1/n_{\text{i}}^2)$. Each series ends on one level: $n_{\text{f}} = 1$ for the Lyman series in the ultraviolet, 2 for the Balmer series that reaches into the visible, and 3 for the Paschen series in the infrared. The formula was found to fit the data before Bohr’s theory derived it.
statements.bohr-transition-energy: Bohr proposed that the orbits of an atom are quantized and that an electron moves between them by absorbing or emitting a photon whose energy is exactly the difference between the two orbital energies, $\Delta E = hf = E_{\text{i}} - E_{\text{f}}$. A quantized set of orbits gives a quantized set of photons, which is a discrete spectrum.
statements.energy-level-diagram: An energy-level diagram is read and drawn by plotting the allowed energies of a system vertically, the ground state at the bottom, and drawing each transition as an arrow between two levels.
statements.bohr-angular-momentum-quantization: Bohr assumed that the angular momentum of an electron in its orbit can take only whole multiples of $h/2\pi$, $L = m_{\text{e}}vr_n = nh/2\pi$. With this rule and the physics of circular motion he calculated the spectrum of hydrogen.
statements.bohr-orbit-radii: Setting the Coulomb force equal to the centripetal force, with the speed from the quantized angular momentum, gives the radius of every allowed orbit of a hydrogen-like atom, $r_n = (n^2/Z)a_{\text{B}}$. The radii grow as $n^2$, and the smallest, the Bohr radius, agrees with the measured size of hydrogen.
statements.ionization-energy: The energy needed to ionize an atom from level $n$ is the size of $E_n$, since an electron at zero energy is free: 13.6 eV from the ground state of hydrogen, less from an excited state. Any energy beyond that goes into the freed electron’s kinetic energy.
statements.limits-of-bohr-theory: Bohr’s theory explains the spectrum and the size of hydrogen and shows that orbital energies and angular momentum are quantized. But its orbits are semiclassical, quantized yet imagined as circles, and it cannot treat an atom with two electrons or explain doublets.
statements.bremsstrahlung-and-characteristic-x-rays: An x-ray tube produces two kinds of radiation at once. Electrons slowing in the anode give a broad, smooth curve of braking radiation, and electrons that knock out inner-shell electrons give sharp peaks characteristic of the anode material.
statements.x-ray-maximum-energy: The most energetic x ray a tube can make is the one for which an electron’s whole kinetic energy becomes a single photon, $E_{\text{max}} = hf_{\text{max}} = q_{\text{e}}V$. A 100-kV tube makes photons of at most 100 keV.
statements.characteristic-x-ray-energy: A characteristic x-ray energy is estimated from hydrogen-like levels with an effective charge of $Z - 1$, since inner electrons feel nearly the whole nucleus. The label names the shell with the vacancy and the shell the electron came from: $K_\alpha$ for $n = 2$ to $n = 1$, $K_\beta$ for $n = 3$ to $n = 1$.
statements.x-ray-diffraction: X-ray diffraction is a technique that finds the arrangement of atoms in a crystal from the pattern of x rays diffracted by its regular rows of atoms, which is possible because an x ray’s wavelength is about the size of an atom.
statements.color-from-energy-levels: The photon energies its atoms can absorb set the color of a material. A tomato looks red because its pigment has levels for every visible photon energy except red, and air is transparent because visible photons find almost no levels to excite in its molecules.
statements.fluorescence: Fluorescence is the process in which an atom excited by a photon of a given energy comes down in smaller steps and emits photons of lower energy, some of them visible. Black lights, glowing minerals and the fluorescent tube work this way.
statements.metastable-state-and-phosphorescence: Most excited states decay in about $10^{-8}$ s, but metastable states live for milliseconds to hours. Their slow decay is phosphorescence, the glow of a luminous dial, and the metastable state is also what makes a laser possible.
statements.population-inversion: A population inversion is the condition in which the majority of the atoms in a sample are in a metastable excited state. A laser needs it, because a photon is as likely to be absorbed by an atom below as to stimulate one above.
statements.stimulated-emission: In stimulated emission a photon passing an atom in an excited state triggers it to emit a second photon with the same energy, phase, polarization and direction, so one photon becomes two, two become four, and the light builds up in step.
statements.laser: A laser, light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation, puts population inversion and stimulated emission together between two mirrors, so that the light passes through the lasing material many times. Its output is a single wavelength and coherent.
statements.wavelength-from-a-level-spacing: The wavelength of a photon emitted or absorbed between two levels is found from the difference between their energies in electron volts, with $\lambda = hc/\Delta E$ and $hc = 1240$ eV·nm.
statements.holography: Holography records the interference of coherent laser light from an object with light falling directly on the film. Lit again by the same kind of laser, the film acts like a set of diffraction gratings and rebuilds the light from the object, so the image changes with the viewpoint as the object would.
statements.angular-momentum-quantization-from-waves: Putting the de Broglie wavelength into the standing-wave condition gives exactly the quantization of angular momentum that Bohr assumed, $L = m_{\text{e}}vr_n = nh/2\pi$. It also explains why the electron cannot spiral into the nucleus: there is a lowest orbit where the wave can fit.
statements.probability-cloud: Because the electron is a wave, it has no well-defined orbit. Each measurement finds it at a definite place, but repeated measurements build up a cloud of probability, densest near the Bohr radius for the ground state of hydrogen.
statements.zeeman-effect: The Zeeman effect is the splitting of a spectral line into three, five or more lines by an external magnetic field, with a spacing that grows in proportion to the field. It shows that each orbit has several discrete energies in a field instead of one.
statements.orbital-magnetic-field: An orbiting electron is a small current loop, and it makes a magnetic field along its axis, the same line as its orbital angular momentum. An external field exerts a torque on the loop, so an orbit tilted to the field has a different energy from one aligned with it.
statements.space-quantization: Space quantization is the fact that orbital angular momentum can have only certain directions: since the Zeeman lines are discrete, the energies of the tilted orbits are discrete, and the angular momentum can make only certain angles with the field.
statements.intrinsic-spin: The electron has an intrinsic angular momentum, its spin, and with it an intrinsic magnetic field that can point at only one of two angles to another field, spin up or spin down. The two directions have different energies, so spectral lines are doublets even with no external field.
statements.principal-quantum-number: The values of quantized quantities are labeled by quantum numbers. The principal quantum number $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ labels the basic states of a system and sets the energy of the hydrogen atom and its orbital radii.
statements.orbital-angular-momentum-magnitude: The magnitude of an electron’s orbital angular momentum is $L = \sqrt{l(l+1)}\,h/2\pi$, where the angular momentum quantum number $l$ runs from 0 to $n - 1$. In the ground state $l$ is zero, so the ground state of hydrogen has no angular momentum.
statements.z-component-of-angular-momentum: The component of orbital angular momentum along the $z$-axis can take only the values $L_z = m_l h/2\pi$, with $m_l$ running from $-l$ to $l$ in steps of one. Each value of $m_l$ has a different energy in a magnetic field.
statements.angle-of-angular-momentum: The allowed angles between angular momentum and the $z$-axis follow from $\cos\theta = L_z/L$, since $L_z$ is one side of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is $L$. The vectors lie on cones about the axis.
statements.spin-quantum-numbers: The electron’s spin is quantized in magnitude and direction as its orbital angular momentum is, but with the one value $s = 1/2$: $S = \sqrt{s(s+1)}\,h/2\pi$, and its $z$-component is $S_z = m_s h/2\pi$ with $m_s = \pm 1/2$. The state of an electron in an atom is fully given by $(n, l, m_l, m_s)$.
statements.allowed-quantum-numbers: The allowed sets of quantum numbers follow from four rules: $n$ is a positive integer, $l$ runs from 0 to $n - 1$, $m_l$ from $-l$ to $l$, and $m_s$ is $\pm 1/2$. With them you can list the allowed sets for a given $n$ and say which rule a forbidden set breaks.
statements.pauli-exclusion-principle: No two electrons can have the same set of quantum numbers; that is, no two electrons can be in the same state. This is why atoms are not all crowded into their ground states and why only two electrons fit in the $n = 1$ level.
statements.shells-and-subshells: Spectroscopic notation such as $2p^3$ gives the shell, the subshell and the number of electrons in it, with the subshells written $s$, $p$, $d$, $f$ for $l = 0, 1, 2, 3$.
statements.subshell-capacity: Once $l$ is known there are $2l + 1$ values of $m_l$, each with two values of $m_s$, so a subshell can hold at most $2(2l + 1)$ electrons: 2 in an $s$ subshell, 6 in a $p$, 10 in a $d$.
statements.shell-capacity: Adding the subshells of a shell gives at most $2n^2$ electrons: 2 in the first shell, 8 in the second, 18 in the third, 32 in the fourth. These are the lengths from which the periods of the periodic table are built.

new.name: Cathode-ray tube
new.statement: A cathode-ray tube is a vacuum tube containing a source of electrons and a screen on which their beam makes a visible spot.

new.name: Rydberg constant, $R = 1.097 \times 10^{7}$ m⁻¹
new.statement: The Rydberg constant, $R = 1.097 \times 10^{7}$ m⁻¹, is the measured constant that sets the scale of the wavelengths of hydrogen’s spectrum.

new.name: Energy-level diagram
new.statement: An energy-level diagram is a diagram of the allowed energies of the electrons of an atom, or of any system, drawn as horizontal lines one above another.

new.name: Bohr radius, $\kaB = 0.529 \times 10^{-10}$ m
new.statement: The Bohr radius, $a_{\text{B}} = h^2/4\pi^2 m_{\text{e}} k q_{\text{e}}^2 = 0.529 \times 10^{-10}$ m, is the mean radius of the orbit of the electron of a hydrogen atom in its ground state.

new.name: Hydrogen-like atom
new.statement: A hydrogen-like atom is any atom, or ion, with only a single electron.

new.name: Atomic number $Z$
new.statement: The atomic number $Z$ of an atom is the number of protons in its nucleus.

new.name: Metastable state
new.statement: A metastable state is an excited state whose lifetime is at least an order of magnitude longer than that of the most short-lived states.

new.name: Phosphorescence
new.statement: Phosphorescence is the slow de-excitation of a metastable state, a glow that continues after the excitation stops.

new.name: Atomic excitation
new.statement: Atomic excitation is a state in which an atom or ion has acquired the energy to promote one or more of its electrons to higher energy levels.

new.name: Atomic de-excitation
new.statement: Atomic de-excitation is the process by which an atom passes from an excited electronic state back to the ground state, usually by emitting photons.

new.name: Hologram
new.statement: A hologram, from the Greek for entire picture, is a film that records the interference of light from an object with a reference beam, from which a three-dimensional image of the object can be rebuilt.

new.name: Fine structure
new.statement: Fine structure is the splitting of the lines of the hydrogen spectrum, seen when they are examined at very high resolution, into closely spaced doublets.

new.name: Intrinsic magnetic field
new.statement: The intrinsic magnetic field is the magnetic field produced by the intrinsic spin of an electron.

new.name: Orbital angular momentum
new.statement: Orbital angular momentum is the angular momentum of an electron that corresponds to the quantum analog of classical angular momentum, from its motion about the nucleus.

new.name: Quantum number
new.statement: A quantum number is a value that labels the allowed values of a quantized quantity, such as energy or angular momentum.

new.name: Angular momentum quantum number $l$
new.statement: The angular momentum quantum number $l$ labels the magnitude of an electron’s orbital angular momentum and takes the integer values from 0 to $n - 1$.

new.name: Spin quantum number $s$
new.statement: The spin quantum number $s$ labels the magnitude of a particle’s intrinsic spin angular momentum; for electrons $s = 1/2$.

new.name: Spin projection quantum number $m_s$
new.statement: The spin projection quantum number $m_s$ labels the component of a particle’s intrinsic spin along the $z$-axis; for electrons it is $+1/2$ or $-1/2$.

new.name: Intrinsic spin angular momentum, $\kSspin = \sqrt{s(s+1)}\,h/2\pi$
new.statement: The magnitude of the intrinsic, or internal, spin angular momentum of an electron is $S = \sqrt{s(s+1)}\,h/2\pi$.

new.name: $z$-component of spin, $\kSz = m_s h/2\pi$
new.statement: The $z$-component of spin angular momentum is the component of an electron’s intrinsic spin along the $z$-axis, $S_z = m_s h/2\pi$.

new.name: Shell
new.statement: A shell is the probability cloud of the electrons that share a single principal quantum number $n$.

new.name: Subshell
new.statement: A subshell is the probability cloud of the electrons within a shell that share a single angular momentum quantum number $l$.
